name: Documentation Creator
description: An agent that creates project documentation including README files and API docs, and validates the output format for correctness and completeness.

readme-generation.description: Generates well-structured README files with standard sections (title, description, installation, usage, contributing, license)

tests.description: Generated README contains all standard sections
tests.prompt: Create a README.md for a Node.js REST API project called 'task-tracker' that manages tasks with CRUD operations. The project uses Express and MongoDB.

tests.description: README includes code blocks with usage examples
tests.prompt: Create a README.md for a Python CLI tool called 'csvmerge' that merges multiple CSV files. It uses argparse for argument parsing.

tests.description: Output is valid markdown with proper heading hierarchy
tests.prompt: Generate a README for a Rust library called 'fastcache' that provides an in-memory LRU cache. Include installation via Cargo, basic usage, and API overview.

api-documentation.description: Generates API documentation with endpoint descriptions, request/response schemas, and example payloads

tests.description: API documentation lists endpoints with HTTP methods and paths
tests.prompt: Generate API documentation for a user management service with endpoints: POST /users (create), GET /users/:id (get by id), PUT /users/:id (update), DELETE /users/:id (delete). Each accepts/returns JSON.

tests.description: API docs include request and response examples or schemas
tests.prompt: Write API documentation for a POST /orders endpoint that accepts a JSON body with fields: productId (string), quantity (integer), shippingAddress (object with street, city, zip). It returns the created order with an id and status field.

tests.description: API documentation includes HTTP status codes
tests.prompt: Document a GET /products/:id endpoint that returns a product object. Include error responses for not found and server errors.

format-validation.description: Validates that generated documentation follows proper formatting rules and structural conventions

tests.description: Identifies and reports missing required sections in a documentation file
tests.prompt:
Review this README and identify what's missing:

# MyApp

A cool app.

## Installation

npm install myapp

That's it!

tests.description: Generated documentation does not contain placeholder text like TODO or TBD
tests.prompt: Create a complete README.md for a Go web framework called 'swiftserve' that provides routing, middleware, and template rendering. Do not leave any placeholders.

tests.description: Agent always produces non-empty documentation output
tests.prompt: Generate a brief API reference for a single endpoint: GET /health that returns {"status": "ok"}.

contextual-accuracy.description: Documentation accurately reflects the project context, technology stack, and specifics provided by the user

tests.description: Documentation references the correct technologies and tools specified by the user
tests.prompt: Create a README for a TypeScript React application called 'dashboard-pro' that uses Vite for building, Zustand for state management, and Tailwind CSS for styling. It deploys to Vercel.

tests.description: Documentation does not invent features or dependencies not mentioned by the user
tests.prompt: Write a minimal README for a Python script called 'hello.py' that prints 'Hello World'. It has no dependencies, no installation steps, and no configuration. Just describe what it does and how to run it.

tests.description: Documentation structure adapts to the type of project (library vs application vs CLI tool)
tests.prompt: Create a README for an npm library called 'string-utils' that exports functions: capitalize, slugify, truncate. It's meant to be used as a dependency in other projects.
